clue.text: Therapist in employment following stroke

indicators.note: the employment word is placed after the stroke word, so following sets the order of the two parts

blocks.note: a massé is a stroke in billiards played with a steeply angled cue
use, as in putting something to work

explanation.surface: A therapist gets back to work after having a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' suggests illness, but it is the billiards shot called a massé.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseuse is a woman whose professional treatment is massage, a kind of physical therapy.

clue.text: Satisfied garaging Welsh runner’s old banger?

indicators.note: garaging means housing something, so the river goes inside the other word

blocks.note: met, as a need or demand is met
the Usk is a river in Wales; a river runs

explanation.surface: A happy owner keeps a Welshman's old car in the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for an old car, but here it is something that goes bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A musket is a muzzle-loading gun of old, so jocularly an antique thing that fires with a bang.

clue.text: Rum and raisin for Italian islander

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters come out in a peculiar order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An islander from Italy is served rum and raisin ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink in a rum and raisin flavour; it is the adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sardinian is a native of Sardinia, a large island belonging to Italy.

clue.text: Controversial eastern cause

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
a motive is the reason or cause behind an act

explanation.surface: An Eastern political cause stirs controversy.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotive issue arouses strong feeling, so it tends to be hotly disputed.

clue.text: Divine direction initially sourced in bishop’s office

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word beside it
the two letters sit inside the word for the bishop's office

blocks.note: N for north, a compass direction
the first letter of sourced
a see is a bishop's diocese or seat

explanation.surface: Guidance from God is traced to a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective about God; it is the verb meaning to perceive by intuition.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine something is to perceive or grasp it intuitively, which is to sense it.

clue.text: Printing office in place with hard ground

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed and broken up, so the letters are reduced and reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A printing works stands on a site with hard, compacted ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like soil but is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapel is the traditional name for a printing house or its workers' union branch, a trade sense.

clue.text: Toast and greeting succeeded with Conservative

blocks.note: a casual greeting
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Raising a glass and saying hello at a Conservative success party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' suggests a drink's salute, but here it is slang for finished.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, someone who is toast is done for, and so is someone who is history.

clue.text: Parking on narrow road for flat surface

indicators.note: on places the parking letter directly before the road word

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: Parking on a narrow road needs a level patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a plane is a perfectly level two-dimensional expanse.

clue.text: At sea, if able to, this saves people

definitions.text: At sea, if able to, this saves people

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Out on the water, whenever possible, this craft rescues people.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeboat is a vessel launched to rescue people in danger on the water.

clue.text: Slap raised lump on skin without discomfort

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a wart is a small raised growth on the skin
pain is discomfort

explanation.surface: A slap raised a painless lump on someone's skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Slap is British slang for make-up, not a blow; 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is jocular slang for make-up, just as slap is theatrical slang for it.

clue.text: Debauchee’s son, Irish, can start to swim in two rivers

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
the swimming letter is placed inside the pair of river names

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
IR is a short form of Irish
can and john are both slang words for a toilet
the Fal is a river in Cornwall
the opening letter of swim
the Taff is a river in Wales, the second of the two

explanation.surface: A dissolute Irishman's son can go swimming between two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Falstaff is the classic drinker and rake; can means toilet, as john does in American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat, drunken knight, the stage archetype of a dissolute pleasure-seeker.

clue.text: Building stone at last provided in numbered blocks?

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the preceding word only
the condition word sits inside the word for numbered blocks

blocks.note: the final letter of stone
provided that means if
dice are small cubes marked with numbers

explanation.surface: A building put together from stone and numbered blocks, like a child's construction set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provided' is the conjunction meaning on condition that, and numbered blocks are dice, not building bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing construction such as a grand house or monument.

clue.text: “Saw” for “see” say

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
see is an example of a part of speech that names an action

explanation.surface: A grammar note: one word may be written in place of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is the noun meaning an old saying; 'say' marks see as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old, often-repeated saying, a maxim of folk wisdom.

clue.text: Line with repetition, not on for learned people

indicators.note: not on asks for those two letters to be left out of the word before it

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
iteration is the act of doing something again

explanation.surface: A teacher's advice: learn lines by repeating them, which suits scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: ITERATION loses its ON to leave ITERATI.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read, educated people interested in literature and scholarship.

clue.text: Leader in west becoming a calamity?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is the one marked for replacing
becoming means turning into something else, so the first letter is swapped

blocks.note: the Occident is the West
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leader in the West turning into a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader in west' means the first letter of the word for west, which becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unexpected mishap, which at its worst is a disaster.

clue.text: Agent on vacation was resting around Crimean resort

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inside of the word goes and only its ends stay
turned around, the joined words read from right to left

blocks.note: the first and last letters of agent
lay is the past tense of lie, to rest

explanation.surface: A spy on holiday lay lounging around a Black Sea resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta is a seaside town on the Crimean coast, famous for the 1945 Allied conference.

clue.text: Luxurious vehicle minus oil: engine’s head cracked

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
something cracked is broken, so the letters are scattered and reset

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of engine

explanation.surface: A posh car has run out of oil and its cylinder head has cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minus' is not a subtraction signal here; its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large, chauffeur-driven luxury car.

clue.text: Creature a tailless sort — positive about that?

indicators.note: without a tail, the word loses its final letter
about means surrounding, so the positive word goes around the rest

blocks.note: a plus is a positive
taken as written
a type is a sort or kind

explanation.surface: Asking whether an animal of a sort without a tail is a good thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is an egg-laying Australian mammal, an odd animal with a duck-like bill.

clue.text: Knightly weapon for Percival perhaps?

definitions.note: a first name that goes with the surname Percival

blocks.note: first meaning: the long spear used by mounted knights
second meaning: the first name of ... Percival, a British comic actor of the 1960s

explanation.walkthrough: Percival suggests Sir Perceval of the Round Table, but here it is a surname needing a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is the jousting spear of chivalry, and Lance is also the given name of the entertainer Percival.

clue.text: Obvious competition among papers? On the contrary

indicators.note: among says one thing sits inside another
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the papers sit inside instead

blocks.note: an event is a contest in a sports programme
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Is the contest among the newspapers plain to see? Apparently not.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the competition would go inside the papers; 'on the contrary' reverses which word holds which. Papers means identity documents, not newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plainly visible or clear to the eye or mind.

clue.text: Subterranean excavation in which animal needs grooming?

blocks.note: a cat is an animal
an animal needing grooming needs a comb

explanation.surface: An underground chamber where a scruffy animal is waiting to be groomed.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery cut into rock, with tunnels and recesses for tombs.

clue.text: Keeping key articles out of American daily?

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: C is a musical key
a and a, two indefinite articles
USA Today is a US national newspaper

explanation.surface: A crucial article is missing from an American newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Custody is the care or protective keeping of someone or something.

clue.text: United in mess — bust possibly

indicators.note: the united letter is placed inside the word for mess

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for United in football team names
a state, as in what a state the room is in

explanation.surface: A football club in a mess is possibly bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like bankrupt, but it is a sculpted head and shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a sculpture of the head and shoulders, one kind of statue.

clue.text: Jack, one opening wine, stayed behind

indicators.note: the one opens up the wine word and sits inside it

blocks.note: jack and tar are both old words for a sailor
the Roman numeral for one
red wine

explanation.surface: A sailor opens a bottle of wine and lingers after everyone else has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarried means lingered or waited about rather than leaving promptly.

clue.text: Made-to-measure item for Mikado?

blocks.note: first meaning: a straight-edged strip made for measuring
second meaning: the Mikado was the emperor of Japan

explanation.walkthrough: 'Made-to-measure' suggests tailoring, but here it means made for measuring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler measures lengths, and a ruler is also a sovereign such as the Japanese emperor.

clue.text: Bellow for example in a way that brings violence?

indicators.note: the novelist's first name is placed inside the words for a way

blocks.note: Saul Bellow was an American novelist
A plus ST, the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Shouting in a certain manner can lead to violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bellow' looks like a shout, but it is the writer Saul Bellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent physical attack on someone, an act of violence.

clue.text: Gold put in stove makes coin

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the gold goes within the stove

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
an Aga is a British brand of cast-iron range cooker

explanation.surface: Melting gold in a stove turns it into a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora is a small Israeli coin, a hundredth of a shekel.

clue.text: Make changes to stop allegation restricting old scientist

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the old letter goes inside
changes made to the letters rework them into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to rework their claim so it stops limiting an old scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaeontologist is a scientist who studies fossils and ancient forms of life.

clue.text: Right to have hard feelings about water pixie

indicators.note: the feelings word holds the right letter inside it, as to have suggests possession
about means surrounding, so the feelings word wraps the other letter

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
spite is ill will or resentment

explanation.surface: It's right for someone to bear a grudge against a water spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or fairy, and water sprites are a traditional kind of nature spirit.

clue.text: Satellite states in America

blocks.note: Georgia
New York
Maine
Delaware

explanation.surface: Political satellite states sit within America's sphere.
explanation.walkthrough: Four postal codes for US states run together.
